questions.stem: What is an opiate?
options: A fully synthetic drug with no receptor activity
A naturally occurring substance with morphine-like actions
A drug that reverses respiratory depression
A partial mu agonist used only for mild pain

questions.stem: How does the term opioid differ from opiate?
questions.answer: Opioid is the wider term, including synthetic drugs with affinity for opioid receptors

questions.stem: How many chemical classes do Group 1 (naturally occurring) opioids have?
What defines a Group 2 (semisynthetic) opioid?
options: Found unchanged in the opium poppy
Built entirely from non-opioid chemical structures

questions.stem: What is the structural class of Group 3 opioids?
What usually causes a rash after morphine?
options: Excess mu receptor stimulation in skin
Direct skin toxicity from the parent drug

questions.stem: How common is true anaphylaxis to opioids?
After a true opioid allergy, how should the replacement opioid be chosen?
options: The same opioid at a lower dose
Any opioid from the same chemical group
The oral form of the same drug

questions.stem: Which two opioid groups are structurally close, so avoid both after a true allergy to one?
Why can Group 3 synthetic opioids usually be given after a true allergy to a Group 1 opioid?
options: They are the same drug class, so cross-react less
They are given in doses too low to trigger allergy
They are structurally different enough to avoid cross-reactivity
They are given only by the epidural route

questions.stem: Which type of mu receptor binding is best for acute pain?
Why are partial opioid agonists of limited use for pain?
options: Full mu receptor binding at all doses

questions.stem: What receptor profile defines agonist-antagonist opioids?
Which receptors do opioids act on in brain and spinal cord, mimicking endorphins?
Which opioid action gives the most potent clinical analgesia?
What class of receptor are opioid receptors?
Which opioid is available as a transdermal patch?
Which plasma proteins partly bind opioids?
Which form of an opioid does the receptor bind?
What mainly ends the effect of opioids (offset)?
options: Biliary excretion of the parent drug

questions.stem: In renal failure, which opioids does impaired clearance matter most for?
questions.answer: Meperidine, morphine, hydromorphone and their prodrugs

questions.stem: Which polymorphic liver enzyme matters more clinically for codeine?
Which body size measure best relates to opioid clearance for dosing?
How should opioid doses change in haemorrhagic shock?
options: Double the dose for faster onset

questions.stem: By when does opioid elimination normalise in neonates?
Why are opioids eliminated more slowly in neonates?
questions.answer: Immature metabolism, including CYP450 activity

questions.stem: What are the few absolute contraindications to opioids?
options: Chronic renal failure of any degree

questions.stem: Most opioid contraindications are relative; what is their main type?
Anaesthetic effects of opioids: they give analgesia and sedation but no reliable ____.
questions.answer: amnesia

questions.stem: Why does the benefit and side-effect profile of opioids vary between patients?
options: Mainly differences in the local anaesthetic used
Only differences in patient body mass
Only the dose given per kilogram

questions.stem: Which two cardiovascular effects do opioids cause by raising vagal tone?
How does opioid direct myocardial depression compare with many IV and inhaled anaesthetics?
What is the overall direct effect of opioids on cardiac rhythm?
How do high-dose opioids compare with volatile agents for myocardial oxygen balance?
options: As well as or better than volatiles

questions.stem: What vascular effect do opioids have?
options: Mild systemic vasodilation, possibly pulmonary vasodilation

questions.stem: Which two stress-response pathways do opioids blunt?
In which situation are opioids useful for haemodynamic stability?
options: When the patient is hypothermic only
When cardiac output must be raised
Only for patients already on inotropes

questions.stem: What is the most serious adverse effect of opioids?
How do opioids change the ventilatory response to carbon dioxide?
options: Increased, with a lower apnoeic threshold
Unchanged, with a lower end-tidal CO2
Reduced, with a higher apnoeic threshold and higher end-tidal CO2
Unchanged, with a higher apnoeic threshold

questions.stem: Why can supplemental oxygen deepen opioid respiratory depression?
options: It raises the CO2 response above normal
It removes the hypoxic stimulus to breathing
It blocks the CO2 response directly

questions.stem: In up to what share of patients does an IV bolus of fentanyl, sufentanil or alfentanil cause brief cough?
Which IV opioid boluses can cause brief cough?
questions.answer: Fentanyl, sufentanil and alfentanil

questions.stem: Which opioid most often causes bronchospasm through histamine release?
What do opioids tend to do to cerebral blood flow alongside vasodilating anaesthetics or N2O?
options: No change in cerebral blood flow

questions.stem: What is the effect of opioids on intracranial pressure with controlled ventilation?
Which opioid-related activity can raise regional cerebral metabolism?
Is there a seizure risk from opioids at normal doses in patients without epilepsy?
options: No risk at normal doses without epilepsy
High risk even at normal doses

questions.stem: Are intraoperative opioids a risk factor for postoperative nausea and vomiting?
Where do opioids act to cause nausea, and through which receptors?
questions.answer: Chemoreceptor trigger zone, via 5-HT3 and dopamine receptors

questions.stem: How do opioids affect gastric emptying and bowel transit?
questions.answer: Slow gastric emptying and transit, causing constipation and ileus

questions.stem: What urinary effect does mu receptor activation by opioids cause?
What urinary effect does kappa receptor activation by opioids cause?
options: Urinary retention with marked sodium loss

questions.stem: What is the general effect of opioids on renal function?
questions.answer: Largely preserved; changes are secondary to systemic and renal haemodynamics

questions.stem: Which opioid route especially causes urinary retention?
questions.answer: Intrathecal opioids

questions.stem: What do opioids do to ureteric tone?
What postoperative effect can high-dose intraoperative remifentanil have?
options: A small but significant rise in postoperative pain

questions.stem: What may contribute to opioid-induced hyperalgesia?
What happens after remifentanil at 2.5 ng/mL for 30 minutes is stopped abruptly?
Which remifentanil weaning regime avoided hyperalgesia?
What is the probable mechanism of opioid-induced hyperalgesia?
options: Sensitisation of pronociceptive pathways, probably NMDA receptor involvement
Direct blockade of antinociceptive pathways only

questions.stem: Which drug supports an NMDA role in opioid-induced hyperalgesia?
Which COX-2 inhibitor, given before remifentanil, suggested COX-2 involvement in hyperalgesia?
What chronic problem is opioid-induced hyperalgesia linked to?
Does histamine release explain opioid-induced pruritus?
options: Yes, histamine release is the sole cause
No, non-histamine-releasing opioids also cause it
Yes, but only with intrathecal use
No, it is caused only by naloxone

questions.stem: After which opioid routes is pruritus worst?
How may antihistamines help with opioid-induced pruritus?
questions.answer: Possibly through sedation

questions.stem: Why is naloxone a poor choice for treating opioid-induced pruritus?
Why are nalbuphine and butorphanol increasingly used for opioid-induced pruritus?
questions.answer: Partial mu antagonism with kappa analgesia kept

questions.stem: In pregnancy, maternal opioids reduce fetal heart rate ____.
questions.answer: variability

questions.stem: What milk-to-plasma ratio do fentanyl and morphine reach in breast milk?
Under anaesthesia, how far do opioids probably lower thermoregulatory thresholds?
questions.answer: About as much as volatile agents

questions.stem: Why do opioids constrict the pupil?
questions.answer: They remove inhibition of the Edinger-Westphal nucleus

questions.stem: Which hormones fall with opioid administration?
questions.answer: LH, testosterone, oestradiol and oxytocin

questions.stem: How do opioids affect sphincter of Oddi tone and bile duct pressure?
questions.answer: Both increase, usually with little clinical consequence

questions.stem: What effect can opioids have on sleep after surgery?
questions.answer: They can disrupt sleep on the first postoperative night

questions.stem: What is the suspected cause of opioid-induced hallucinations?
questions.answer: Possibly dopamine dysregulation

questions.stem: How do opioids affect sensory and motor evoked potentials?
What possible benefit do opioids have in liver surgery?
questions.answer: May reduce ischaemia-reperfusion injury

questions.stem: What does animal data suggest about teratogenicity of fentanyl, sufentanil and alfentanil?
questions.answer: Appears minimal in animals

questions.stem: Which babies are at risk of neonatal abstinence syndrome after maternal opioid exposure?
questions.answer: Babies of mothers with opioid use disorder or on prescribed opioids

questions.stem: Which opioids at induction help prevent a rise in intraocular pressure?
What does epidemiology suggest about cancer recurrence after opioid-based anaesthesia?
questions.answer: More recurrence than after local anaesthesia or regional techniques

questions.stem: In opioid overdose, which sedation finding defines oversedation?
What respiratory rate defines hypoventilation in opioid overdose?
What is the full adult IV naloxone dose for opioid overdose?
What is the highest IV naloxone dose used to diagnose adult opioid overdose?
After naloxone wears off in opioid overdose, what should happen to the patient?
questions.answer: Observe until awake

questions.stem: With long-acting opioids, a naloxone infusion may be needed for up to ____.
What can cause renarcotisation after naloxone in opioid overdose?
questions.answer: Any agonist with a longer half-life than naloxone

questions.stem: Where do secondary peaks in opioid plasma levels come from?
questions.answer: Release from muscle, lung, fat and gut

questions.stem: What does opioid tolerance mean for the analgesia from a fixed dose?
options: More analgesia over time, so doses fall
Less analgesia over time, so doses escalate
Faster onset of analgesia each dose
Same analgesia but a longer duration

questions.stem: How is physiological dependence on opioids shown?
questions.answer: Withdrawal when the drug is stopped abruptly

questions.stem: What are the early symptoms of opioid withdrawal?
questions.answer: Irritability, anxiety, insomnia, sweating, yawning, rhinorrhoea and lacrimation

questions.stem: What later symptoms occur in opioid withdrawal?
questions.answer: Fever, chills, myalgia, abdominal cramps, diarrhoea and tachycardia

questions.stem: How long does opioid withdrawal typically last?
How is opioid addiction defined?
questions.answer: Use causing physical, psychological or social harm, continued despite it

questions.stem: What is known about the mechanisms behind opioid addiction?
questions.answer: Not fully known; genetic, molecular, cellular, physiological and functional factors

questions.stem: How do different opioid effects develop tolerance?
questions.answer: At different rates and to different degrees

questions.stem: Can opioid tolerance develop without chronic use? Give one example.
questions.answer: Yes, acute tolerance, e.g. with remifentanil

questions.stem: In chronic high-dose opioid users, how predictable is tolerance for analgesia and respiratory depression?
questions.answer: Hard to predict

questions.stem: Which of these is not a classical (naloxone-sensitive) opioid receptor?
How is the NOP receptor classified within the opioid family?
questions.answer: Non-classical, a non-opioid member of the family

questions.stem: Which opioid receptor mainly mediates clinical opioid analgesia?
questions.answer: MOP

questions.stem: Where do the endogenous opioid peptides for each receptor come from?
questions.answer: Selective peptides cleaved from precursor prohormones

questions.stem: Which endogenous peptides act on MOP receptors?
questions.answer: Beta-endorphin, endomorphin-1 and endomorphin-2

questions.stem: What is the precursor of the MOP peptide beta-endorphin?
questions.answer: Pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC)

questions.stem: Which endogenous peptides act on DOP (delta) receptors?
questions.answer: Met-enkephalin and leu-enkephalin

questions.stem: What is the precursor prohormone of the DOP endogenous peptides?
questions.answer: Pro-enkephalin

questions.stem: Which endogenous peptides act on KOP (kappa) receptors?
questions.answer: Dynorphin A and dynorphin B

questions.stem: What is the endogenous ligand of the NOP receptor?
questions.answer: Nociceptin, or orphanin FQ (N/OFQ)

questions.stem: Where are MOP receptors found in the body?
questions.answer: Throughout the CNS and in peripheral neural and non-neural tissue

questions.stem: Which supraspinal region has dense opioid MOP receptors?
questions.answer: Periaqueductal grey (PAG)

questions.stem: Where in the spinal cord do opioids reduce pain transmission?
questions.answer: Substantia gelatinosa of the dorsal horn

questions.stem: Spinal opioids cut C and Aδ fibre transmission by reducing release of which two transmitters?
questions.answer: Glutamate and substance P

questions.stem: Which opioid effects are driven by peripheral receptors?
questions.answer: Reduced gut motility, urinary retention and pruritus

questions.stem: In opioid mood and reward effects, dopamine is released mainly in which structure?
What type of receptor are the opioid receptors?
questions.answer: Gi-coupled GPCRs

questions.stem: What do opioid receptors do to adenylyl cyclase?
Which potassium channels do opioid receptors open in neurons?
questions.answer: G-protein-gated inwardly rectifying (GIRK) channels

questions.stem: What is the net effect of opioid receptor activation on a neuron?
questions.answer: Less impulse transmission and less transmitter release

questions.stem: Which opioid receptor type causes respiratory depression?
Which neurotransmitter release does MOP activation inhibit?
questions.answer: Acetylcholine

questions.stem: Which effect does delta (DOP) opioid receptor activation produce?
Which effect is linked to kappa (KOP) opioid receptor activation?
How much more potent than fentanyl is sufentanil?
What is sufentanil used for in anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Induction and maintenance
